subject: Itai et al. (2022)
object: Itai et al. (2022) described 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia. All 4 had sharp angulation of the femora and humeri, distinctive facial features, and neonatal respiratory distress. Three had short stature and 3 developed postnatal osteoporosis followed by fractures. Two had brachycephaly and 2 were diagnosed with optic atrophy.

subject: Itai et al. (2022)
object: In 2 of 4 individuals with kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to find a de novo heterozygous c.272A>G variant in the KIF5B gene, which results in a lys91-to-arg (K91R) substitution. The affected amino acid is conserved and lies in or close to the ATPase activity-related motifs of the catalytic motor domain.

subject: Itai et al. (2022)
object: In 1 individual with kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to find a de novo heterozygous c.584C>A variant in the KIF5B gene, which results in a thr195-to-lys (T195K) substitution. The affected amino acid is conserved and lies in or near the ATPase-related motifs of the motor domain.

subject: Itai et al. (2022)
object: In 1 individual with kyphomelic dysplasia, Itai et al. (2022) used whole-exome sequencing to find a de novo heterozygous c.701G>T variant in the KIF5B gene, which results in a gly234-to-val (G234V) substitution. The affected amino acid is conserved and lies in or near the ATPase-related motifs of the motor domain.

subject: Itai et al. (2022)
object: Itai et al. (2022) described kyphomelic dysplasia as a heterogeneous group of skeletal dysplasias with severe bowing of the limbs and other variable features, such as a narrow thorax and abnormal facies. They suggested that heterozygous deleterious KIF5B variants cause a specific form of kyphomelic dysplasia, which extends the phenotypic spectrum of the kinesinopathies.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) injected human KIF5B mRNA carrying the kyphomelic dysplasia-associated p.Thr195Lys (c.584C>A) missense variant into 1-cell zebrafish embryos. By 2 dpf, these embryos had a significant increase in mild and severe heart defects and heart edema. They also had a wider ceratohyal cartilage angle than embryos injected with wildtype KIF5B. Expressing the variant in motoneurons significantly reduced mitochondrial coverage along the axon and caused mitochondrial transport defects. The authors suggested that the variants act as dominant-negative alleles.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) re-reviewed the 4 previously reported patients with KIF5B-related kyphomelic dysplasia, who carried de novo p.Thr195Lys, p.Gly234Val, or p.Lys91Arg variants. All 4 had neonatal distress and respiratory failure, and their hypotonia partially resolved with age. Single individuals had tracheomalacia, glossoptosis, or velopharyngeal insufficiency. Clubfoot was present in 3 of the 4 patients.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) noted that the kyphomelic dysplasia-associated KIF5B variants affect residues Lys91, Thr195, and Gly234. These residues lie in the motor domain and cluster in the pocket that binds ATP/ADP. Joint contractures were seen only in patients with motor-domain variants, which suggested a correlation between altered motor-domain function and joint contractures or clubfoot.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) identified 3 other dominantly acting KIF5B variants located further 3-prime than the kyphomelic dysplasia variants: p.Asn255del at the end of the motor domain, and p.Leu498Pro and p.Leu537Pro in the coiled-coil domain. These caused phenotypes ranging from a syndromic neurodevelopmental disorder to adult-onset dilated cardiomyopathy with ophthalmoplegia and skeletal myopathy, without kyphomelic dysplasia apart from scoliosis in 1 patient. The authors proposed grouping these conditions as KIF5B-related diseases.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) described an Italian boy (subject 1), last evaluated at 8 years 3 months. He had a neurodevelopmental disorder with severe developmental delay and intellectual disability, early-onset refractory epilepsy, and severe hypotonia, and needed a gastrostomy for feeding. He also had progressive cortical atrophy, a thin corpus callosum, and dysmorphic features including bitemporal narrowing, hypertelorism, ptosis, and a short deep philtrum. Severe scoliosis was reported at 9 years.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) used trio whole-exome sequencing in subject 1 and identified a de novo heterozygous c.1610T>C (p.Leu537Pro) variant in KIF5B. The variant was absent from gnomAD and affects a conserved leucine in the coiled-coil dimerization region. Fibroblasts from the patient showed abnormal cilia, enlarged and peripherally located lysosomes, and Golgi disorganization. Motoneurons derived from the patient's iPSCs had reduced mitochondrial coverage in the distal parts of their neurites.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) described a family (family 2) with autosomal dominant, adult-onset dilated cardiomyopathy that required heart transplantation in 3 members. Affected members also had skeletal myopathy that worsened over time, ophthalmoplegia, elevated CPK, joint contractures, and peripheral neuropathy. A heterozygous in-frame deletion in KIF5B, c.765_767delCAA (p.Asn255del), segregated with the disorder; it was inherited from the father of a 67-year-old man (subject 2) and was carried by his 2 affected sisters. Zebrafish embryos injected with this variant developed heart defects.

subject: Flex et al. (2023)
object: Flex et al. (2023) described a 6-year-old girl (subject 3) with mild developmental delay, severe hypotonia that began prenatally, feeding difficulties requiring G-tube feeding, and mild dysmorphism. She carried a de novo heterozygous KIF5B variant, c.1493T>C (p.Leu498Pro), in the coiled-coil domain.
